title: Python async (asyncio), Part 3: TaskGroup, limits, deadlines
tldr: Why two awaits in a row take the sum (seller-a then seller-b: 200 ms, against 120 ms when both are started as Tasks first). Coroutine objects vs Tasks, create_task, gather (argument order, return_exceptions, and the calls it leaves running), TaskGroup and its ExceptionGroup, except*, as_completed and eager tasks, each traced back to Part 2's Futures, done callbacks and timers. Gateway v4 runs the five seller calls in a TaskGroup under one Semaphore shared by every request and one timeout_at deadline per request, entered before the wait for a slot: seller-a to seller-d answer and seller-e is reported as timed out at 250 ms. Then production defaults (HTTPX and aiohttp pools and timeouts), and what breaks at 10 times the load, measured: calls left running after gather fails, 500 calls at once hitting EMFILE and failing the whole group, a timer that starts after the wait for a slot (1,770 ms against a 250 ms budget), and an overloaded seller doing work nobody reads. Ends with gather vs TaskGroup vs as_completed vs wait and an interview drill: call 500 APIs, answer within 1 s, take nothing down.
